title: Universal transport upgrade and legacy response-field sunset playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
We need to safely bump core HTTP/transport dependencies across our Python, JavaScript, and Go SDKs and simultaneously remove two legacy API response fields that have leaked into customer code. Recent dependency upgrades (requests -> 3.x, node-fetch -> 4.x/ESM, and go net/http changes) introduce behavioral changes for some consumers (CJS vs ESM in JS, connection pooling defaults in Python, stricter TLS/handshake expectations in Go). Concurrently we will sunset the legacy response fields 'v1_text' and 'raw_text' in favor of a normalized 'text' + structured 'content' payload. This ticket coordinates cross-language work, defines a canary rollout, adds a short-lived compatibility shim, and provides migration docs and monitoring gates.
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs publish new minor versions with transport bumps and compatibility shims
Automated migration guide published with code snippets for Python/JS/Go
Canary rollout to 5% of hosted API traffic for 72 hours with no customer-facing errors (>=99.9% success) and <5% regression in p95 latency
Deprecation header set on responses and documented in release notes
End-to-end integration tests cover legacy field access and shim behavior
Compatibility shim removed in a follow-up release after one release cycle and communicated via changelog and email
tasks: Audit direct and transitive transport deps in each SDK and lockfiles
Implement per-SDK compatibility shim that maps v1_text/raw_text -> text/content when legacy keys used
Update SDK unit/integration tests to assert both old and new field access paths
Create migration guide (Confluence + quickstart snippets) and sample PR templates for customers
Run load tests comparing old vs bumped transport stacks and capture cpu/latency/delta
Prepare canary rollout plan in Console with routing policy for 5% traffic
Instrument tracing and add dashboard tiles for p50/p95/p99 latency, 4xx/5xx, and token throughput
Publish SDK releases and announce deprecation timeline (90 days)
notes: 2025-02-11: Spike showed requests 3.x changes to connection pooling increased p95 by ~6% in synthetic latency tests for short-lived connections. Root cause: different default adapter settings and reduced keep-alive reuse in some runtime combinations.

2025-02-18: JS ESM-only node-fetch v4 forces downstream bundlers to change import style; CJS consumers will break if not provided a compatibility build. Decided to ship CJS wrapper for one release cycle.

2025-02-22: Go upgrade (go1.20+) tightened TLS negotiation; we observed a 2% CPU uplift in our microbenchmarks for mutual-TLS customers. Add opt-in dialer flag to SDK until we confirm kernel-level settings.
2025-03-01: Product requested clearer messaging about deprecation window and a migration checklist for customer success to use in outreach
canary_plan: Phase 1: Publish SDKs to package registries with 'legacy-shim' enabled by default; tag prereleases for early adopters
Phase 2: Enable new SDKs for internal canary customers and 5% hosted traffic (72h observation window)
Phase 3: If canary passes, ramp to 25% then full rollout over 48 hours; if regressions observed, toggle shim on server-side routing policy to keep affected traffic on older runtime
Phase 4: After 30 days of stable rollout, flip deprecation header to 'will_remove_in_release=sdk-2025.07' and schedule shim removal in next cycle
qa_checklist: Unit tests for old and new field access (Python/JS/Go)
Integration tests hitting hosted API ensuring deprecation header present
Bundle tests for JS to validate CJS wrapper (webpack/rollup/parcel)
Load test with short-lived and long-lived connections to validate keep-alive behavior
Security quick-scan for new dependency versions
Manual verify sample apps on internal dev tenants
rollback_plan: If canary fails (>=0.1% customer errors or >5% p95 regression), immediately disable new SDK release via package advisory and toggle routing policy to route affected traffic to dedicated older runtime. Reopen PRs to revert dependency bump commits and re-run perf/regression tests. Notify customers and CS with incident postmortem timeline.
communication_plan: Draft customer-facing deprecation email and changelog entry (Product owns)
Post migration guide and code snippets to docs site and highlight in release notes
Host 1-hour office hours for top 20 customers identified by usage
Slack announcement in #sdk-updates and #platform-announce on release day
